chapter_title: Concerning the Sect of the Basket
chapter_note: This kephalaion is front-loaded with hagiographic scene-setting and anti-sectarian/application material about “the basket” (¶1–4). The cosmological-teaching substrate appears only in the broken fragments of ¶5–6 (pillars, angels, cosmic supports, Living Spirit garments, Porter). ¶5 is especially unstable: a brief institutional phrase (“holy church”) intrudes into an otherwise cosmological enumeration, consistent with the chapter-level fatigue signal.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic narrative container: setting in Babylon, arrival of a presbyter, labels like “our enlightener” and “apostle”; biographical scene-setting rather than cosmological exposition.

Sect-descriptive/etiological explanation of a contemporary group-name (“sect of the ‘basket’”) with mundane fruit-picking imagery; not a cosmos→cosmos mapping but a present-world referent (how they name/handle fruit).

Dialogue attribution (“The apostle speaks…”) plus explicit application to a sectarian identity claim and alms-language. The universe-as-tree analogy is used polemically (“how then do you call yourself…”) and anchors to institutional practice (“alms”), so it functions as editorial application rather than substrate cosmology.
Blessing/exhortation about alms and relocation of goods into “the basket, which is the holy church!”—explicit institutional mapping (cosmic metaphor used to point to church practice).

paragraphs.core_text: The [...] and the great [...] and the great Mind that is [...] this Youth that is with the [...] thirty-six angels [...] twenty-two angels [...] but [...] of the twenty-two [...] ⟨p.290⟩ the seven pillars that stan[d ...] the sea that surrounds the universe [...] four angels that are distributed to the [...] universe, supporting the mightiness [...] below, which is the earth of all the heavens [...] these other five gods, the sons of the Man, they that [...] the universe is stood firm [...] the Summons and the Obedience [...] the splendour of the [...] and the Adamant of Light [...] they are become enemies [...] they guide it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue/frame lead-in (“Then he says to him …”). Removed the institutional insertion “holy church” from the phrase “the splendour of the [...] holy church and the Adamant of Light” because it crosses from cosmic architecture to church identification (cosmos→institution).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying content is enumerative cosmological architecture (Mind/Youth, angelic counts, seven pillars, encircling sea, four supporting angels, earth-of-heavens, sons of the Man, Summons/Obedience). The brief “holy church” phrase is a register-crossing intrusion consistent with late editorial application/fatigue, so the paragraph is treated as a core list with a small institutional graft.

paragraphs.core_text: The third also, [...] below, there are twelve powers standing firm there. However, the number of the twelve images [...] the three great pillars of mightiness that [...] pillars supporting the disk [...] the other three [...] they are the garments that the Living Spirit [...] he put them at that time [...] that threw them, together with [...] which is displayed therein [...] this [...] perfect before [...] great Porter [...] in his power [...] these are the three great [...] against [...] are in the midst of people [...] knows [...] entrusts his soul to them [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, structural cosmology: twelve powers/images; three great pillars; cosmic disk; ‘garments’ of the Living Spirit; Great Porter—i.e., a world-support mechanism list. No citation formulae or institutional identifications; the mention of ‘people/soul’ remains within soteriological mechanics rather than a contemporary church rule.
